messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — sketching a tiny abstraction layer between ModelCatalog and the runtime to unify FP8/INT8/4-bit handling. Goal: single negotiation surface + well-defined fallback semantics. Thoughts?

julie: Nice. Is this to avoid sprinkling quant logic across adapters?

alex: Exactly. Right now adapters and serving runtime both contain bits of precision logic. Proposal is a "Precision Abstraction Layer (PAL)" that: 1) exposes a small API for profile discovery/compat, 2) performs per-request negotiation (requested profile vs runtime capability), 3) returns an execution plan + fallback policy.

ren: Can you show the API shape? Even pseudo? :thinking:

alex: Sure — rough example:
```
GET /models/:id/precision-profile
response: { profiles: ["fp8-a1", "int8-legacy", "4bit-slim"], default: "fp8-a1" }

POST /negotiate
body: { model_id, requested: "fp8-a1", hints: { latency_budget_ms: 20, quality_floor: 0.92 } }
response: { selected: "int8-legacy", reason: "runtime-lacks-fp8-kernels", fallback_plan: { convert_kv_cache: true, quantize_on_load: true } }
```

chao: I like explicit fallback_plan. Two quick concerns: (a) where to keep profile metadata (metrics, degradation estimates), (b) how we version profiles so clients can pin behaviour.

alex: For (a) store metadata in catalog entries (realtime-indexed) + attach degradation estimates from eval jobs (links to eval run ids). (b) Profiles should have semver-like revision + immutable id. e.g., fp8-a1@v2.

samir: How do we surface per-tenant overrides? Customers might require INT8 only for compliance.

alex: PAL would accept policy overrides in the negotiation call (tenant_policy) that take precedence. The runtime still enforces safety — if tenant says INT8-only but model truly fails quality gating, we return an error with remediation steps.

julie: Runtime implications: does PAL live in control plane or as a sidecar next to runtime worker? Latency for negotiation matters for cold requests.

alex: Two deployment modes: 1) control-plane PAL for catalog-heavy operations (profile discovery, rollout), 2) local PAL shim in runtime for per-request negotiation cached decisions. The local shim can revalidate asynchronously.

ren: Telemetry — we need fine-grained signals: selected_profile, fallback_reason, quality_delta_estimate, tokens_at_degradation. Add to request logs.

chao: Also surface a small deterministic hash of negotiation inputs so we can map decisions to profile versions in traces.

ops-bot: Note: the rollout playbook should include canary steps + a kill switch. Add to runbook: feature_flag.pal_enabled, canary_percent, revert_to: model_id@profile. :white_check_mark:

samir: Tests: unit for API + e2e shadow negotiation comparing old path vs PAL (shadow-sample). Also quality regression harness using small prompt set.

alex: Sounds good. Open questions: storage format for fallback_plan (json blob vs structured), how to represent quantization conversion cost in selection heuristic, and UX for SDK (should clients ever request exact kernel types or stick to profile ids?).

julie: My vote: opaque profile ids for SDKs, only ops tooling exposes kernel-level knobs. Keep SDK simple: request profile id + hints.

ren: Timeline? If we aim for a lightweight MVP (profile discovery + local shim negotiation + telemetry), maybe 3 sprints. Full rollout (catalog UI, eval integration, tenant policies) 2-3 months.

alex: OK — I'll drop a short RFC doc with API defs, schema for profile metadata, and an initial migration plan (shadowing for 4 weeks). Action: alex -> create RFC PR by EOD tomorrow. samir/julie/ren/chao -> quick review next 48h.

chao: Great — please include a small example of how legacy adapters will call PAL (we should have an adapter shim snippet).

alex: Will do. Thanks all.
